messages:
support-alex: FYI acme-inc reported a spike of 502s to their Private VPC endpoints starting ~08:10UTC. They say it happened right after our scheduled cert rotation window. Attachment shows TLS handshake errors and our health checks failing.

support-alex: quick summary from their logs: repeated TLS handshake timeout + 'certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate' on the client side.

customer-acmeops: Confirmed — our internal probes to the Redwood ingress started failing after rotation. We can still reach the VIP, but our app logs show verifier errors for intermediate chain. OCSP stapling timed out in our sidecar.

sre-jess: @customer-acmeops can you paste the openssl output from one of the failing hosts? Also do you block outbound egress to arbitrary IPs? OCSP responders are often on different hosts.

customer-acmeops: We run a strict egress allowlist (only whitelisted IPs). Here's a sample:
```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -servername api.internal.acme -connect api.internal.acme:443 -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
139959...'OCSP Response: no response'
140...verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

support-alex: Thanks. Two hypotheses: (1) our rotator uploaded the leaf cert but missed sending the intermediate in the bundle to the customer's endpoint (chain truncated), or (2) the customer's egress allowlist blocked OCSP/AIA fetches so their verifier couldn't fetch intermediate/OCSP causing validation failures.

eng-marco: I pulled the rotator logs for that tenant for the rotation window: rotator-bot:rotation:3129345600 -> uploaded bundle, checksum matches expected. However rotator-bot reported a warning: "staple lookup timed out for ocsp.example-ca.net" and then proceeded. I think OCSP stapling failed at our edge. Example log snippet:
```
[rotator-bot] 2026-03-12T08:05:23Z staple: lookup ocsp.example-ca.net -> timeout
[rotator-bot] 2026-03-12T08:05:24Z upload: bundle.pem (leaf + intermediate?) size=3.2KB
[rotator-bot] 2026-03-12T08:05:24Z warn: uploaded bundle missing stapled ocsp_response
```

sre-jess: That aligns. Two operational issues to check: 1) customer-side egress allowlist blocking OCSP/AIA (causes clients to attempt fetching issuers/OCSP and fail), 2) proxy/HA layer caching older certs (haproxy/nginx keeps old cert in memory after reload sometimes).

support-alex: Customer says they have an allowlist. They only permit egress to a small set and haven't updated it recently.

eng-marco: Steps I'd recommend we try in this order:
1) Ask customer to temporarily allow outbound to OCSP responder hostnames/IPs (ocsp.example-ca.net and aia.example-ca.net) and retry health checks.
2) From their failing host run: `openssl s_client -servername api.internal.acme -connect api.internal.acme:443 -status -showcerts` and capture the full chain.
3) If allowlist change not possible immediately, we can re-run rotation with full chain forced and explicit stapled OCSP response (if available) and then restart the edge proxy to clear any in-memory caches.

support-alex: Customer: can you allow OCSP egress to ocsp.example-ca.net (89.12.34.56) and aia.example-ca.net (89.12.34.57) for a short window and ping back?

customer-acmeops: Ok temporarily opened egress to those two addresses, restarting health checks now.

customer-acmeops: Health checks are green. Service back to normal. Logs show OCSP stapling succeeded after egress opened.

sre-jess: Good — that confirms egress/OCSP was the blocker. Two follow-ups: 1) we should recommend customers include known CA OCSP/AIA endpoints in their allowlist during rotation windows, 2) consider making rotator upload include full intermediate chain + retry stapling if initial lookup times out.

eng-marco: I'll open an internal issue to change rotator behavior: make OCSP stapling retries (3x, backoff) and attach a warning flag if stapling fails but upload still proceeds. Also add a post-rotation probe that validates chain from an external vantage so we catch blocked OCSP earlier.

support-alex: Customer ops — suggest we provide a short KB blurb they can add to their runbook: list of known OCSP/AIA endpoints for common root/intermediate CAs and a sample curl/openssl check. Want me to draft and paste here?

customer-acmeops: Yes please, that would help others on our team.

support-alex: Drafted snippet, feel free to paste into your runbook:
```
# Quick OCSP/chain check
openssl s_client -connect api.internal.acme:443 -servername api.internal.acme -status -showcerts
# Check for 'OCSP Response: good' and that the chain includes intermediate certs.
# Allowlist example (common endpoints):
# ocsp.example-ca.net -> 89.12.34.56
# aia.example-ca.net -> 89.12.34.57
```

rotator-bot: Note: ticket ROT-412 created to add stapling retry and external post-rotation chain validation.

sre-jess: Marking as resolved for now since customer recovered after allowlist update. Recommend adding a 'rotation runbook' entry to the customer onboarding checklist about egress for OCSP/AIA. :white_check_mark:

support-alex: Closing thread — will follow up with KB and ROT-412 updates. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
